Republican.finding: Brunete’s six opening Republican squadrons can be counted by aircraft type. Later Soviet and Republican participation is identifiable.
Republican.open: A dated opening return naming all six squadrons.

Nationalist.finding: The Italian chronology places two Fiat squadrons at the opening and distinguishes the later reinforcements.
Nationalist.open: A dated field return for the third Fiat squadron in the competing opening account.

Allied.finding: The first-day reports distinguish Warsaw’s Pursuit Brigade from the assisting Army Modlin fighters. Dispersing one formation still left Jabłonna exposed.
Allied.open: German losses attributable to each Polish interception.

Axis.finding: Three German bomber Staffeln and the separate fighter sweep can be placed in the opening operation.
Axis.open: A matching German loss and damage return for the encounter.

Allied.finding: Ark Royal fighters interrupted a specific bombing attack near Åndalsnes. The carrier chronology records the incident.
Allied.open: A consistent series of hours of cover at the Narvik anchorage.

Axis.finding: The German naval diary confirms the loss of Königsberg after the Bergen attack and records the crew’s new shore role.
Axis.open: Comparable aircraft loss returns across the Norwegian theatre.

Allied.finding: The Dutch record follows fighters from two fields through refuelling and regrouping at Buiksloot.
Allied.open: French, Belgian, Dutch and British strength and loss returns on the same day.

Axis.finding: The German fighter encounter with three Belgian escorts over Vroenhoven is identifiable.
Axis.open: A receiving-side report measuring the bombers’ effect at the bridge.

Allied.finding: Squadron records distinguish aircraft that departed from units simply listed at a station on 7 September.
Allied.open: A full daily station-by-station reconciliation of serviceable machines and pilots.

Axis.finding: The bomber and escort orders can be read alongside a naval report of fires in four dock systems.
Axis.open: A record linking each damaged dock to a named bomber formation.

Allied.finding: All 74 Allied allocations can be identified across nine roles. The withdrawal has evidence from a patrol and from the supported naval force.
Allied.open: The amount of shipping damage averted by each patrol.

Axis.finding: Fighter Gruppen and strike Staffeln are identifiable and the naval record confirms the loss of Berkeley.
Axis.open: The specific attacking unit responsible for Berkeley and the full bomber and reconnaissance return.

Allied.finding: Timed approach patrols and the port signal show that Ohio reached unloading under fighter cover.
Allied.open: A matching return for the contribution of each patrol to the safe passage.

Axis.finding: Italian records identify the size of one torpedo wave and its escorts. The reconstruction found no hit from that wave.
Axis.open: Ship-by-ship attribution for damage incurred in other attacks on Pedestal.

Allied.finding: The squadron diary dates the change from Malta to Pachino. The v11 western naval plot and Dickman testimony document interruptions during unloading in a separate sector.
Allied.open: A common ship-and-patrol log for the same Pachino watch.

Axis.finding: The ferry command documented the damaged craft and a change of embarkation jetty at Messina.
Axis.open: A matched German craft and Allied sortie record resolving both the attacker and the disputed wrecking time.

Allied.finding: The carrier return identifies the cover supplied at Salerno while shelling kept Montecorvino from replacing it.
Allied.open: A daily matching of shore-based replacements, carrier patrols and the ships supported.

Axis.finding: A dated III./KG 100 attack and the naval account explain why Savannah left the gun line.
Axis.open: Comparable loss and repair returns across all German units in the Salerno phase.

Allied.finding: The return distinguishes four assigned regiments from three equipped ones. Fifth Army named the corps it wanted them to cover.
Allied.open: The 22nd Mechanized Corps diary confirming when that cover arrived and its effect.

Axis.finding: The 22 June fighter readiness return identifies Gruppen and attached Staffeln in the northern sector.
Axis.open: A combat or loss report tying a specific Axis unit to the 46th Regiment flight in the south.

Allied.finding: Soviet air-army holdings during Uranus can be dated and bounded.
Allied.open: A Soviet unit report identifying an interception and the particular German supply flight it affected.

Axis.finding: The quartermaster’s receipt records cargo and food need. The v11 postal report adds a separate service’s accounting for inbound mail.
Axis.open: An outgoing weight manifest, destination dump receipt and unit issue for the same supply lift.

Allied.finding: The northern air army’s first-day sorties can be separated from aircraft committed to the southern strike. Its history acknowledges gaps in ground support.
Allied.open: A receiving corps return for the effect of a specific 5 July attack.

Axis.finding: The southern corps account describes losses to Soviet aviation within the armoured fighting.
Axis.open: A dated loss return separating air attack from artillery and other causes.

Allied.finding: The daytime bridge mission, its aircraft loss and the later mass strike at Bobruisk have distinct accounts.
Allied.open: A measurement of how the bridge attack affected 9th Tank Corps movement.

Axis.finding: Ninth Army’s diary records traffic and telephone interruptions during the encirclement on 27 June.
Axis.open: Attribution of a particular road stoppage to a named Soviet sortie.

Allied.finding: The night army differentiates the Berlin sorties it recorded from the bombers reporting over the target.
Allied.open: Ground evidence for the effect of that night’s fires on a specific defender.

Axis.finding: Soviet crews observed a German response on 25/26 April and the separate German roster identifies earlier stations.
Axis.open: The defending unit’s identity and a German recipient or loss record for the same raid.

Allied.finding: The 6 March escort table identifies the groups and the stages of their work. V11 traces fuel output and aircraft availability in separate series.
Allied.open: An acceptance-to-squadron record connecting newly produced aircraft to a unit’s operational strength.

Axis.finding: German records establish that bombs reached Berlin and identify individual encounters and damage.
Axis.open: Local repair and activity returns showing how that raid affected the particular unit or transport service.

Allied.finding: The October reports separate the B-24s dispatched from those that flew the diversion and identify the escort groups.
Allied.open: A production loss specifically attributable to an individual bomber group.

Axis.finding: Factory records distinguish machinery, stocks and local output. The v11 comparison follows the recovery and records what users experienced.
Axis.open: A monthly series at a single plant with traceable deliveries to one of its customers.

Allied.finding: Photography documents damage at Gotha. National production and fighter strength can now be followed separately across 1944.
Allied.open: Gotha’s own monthly production and deliveries for the affected line.

Axis.finding: The Steyr account distinguishes factory and housing damage. The Fiume mission and its escorts have a separate history.
Axis.open: A matched Austrian defensive return for 24 February and recipient production records.

Allied.finding: The air and ground reports establish patrols over the eastern beaches. The western naval command records cover and the different unloading experience at Utah and Omaha.
Allied.open: A contemporaneous ship and fighter log capable of attributing a defined intervention to one patrol.

Axis.finding: Eight independently dated movements can be distinguished from the reported 21 German reinforcement Gruppen.
Axis.open: A German return naming the 21 on the dates covered by that total.

Allied.finding: The divisional account gives daily recovered tonnage. V11 identifies the Hamilcar contribution, two separate 20 September collections and the late date conflict.
Allied.open: Synchronized loading, drop and collection returns for Market V on 22–23 September and confirmation of loads on the 25th.

Axis.finding: Six German formations prepared for the opening day and the evidence identifies the three that operated.
Axis.open: A matched record linking later interceptions to a particular load and its recipient.

Allied.finding: The Eindhoven returns separate aircraft repaired from those destroyed or beyond repair.
Allied.open: A dated return for the subsequent operational availability of every repaired Typhoon.

Axis.finding: The separate JG 4 narratives and individual Dutch records help distinguish the groups that reached different fields.
Axis.open: A complete aircraft-level crosswalk between German claims and defenders’ losses.
